title: Machine learning guided design of strong transcriptional activation domains
summary: Computationally generated 500,000 candidate activation domains, scored them with neural-network models, and tested 18,750 in yeast; over 90% of 16,770 well-measured sequences functioned as activation domains. Sequences predicted active by several models were stronger, leading to the consensus predictor MADRIGAL; some designs kept activity in fungi, plants and human cells.
ai_technology: Neural-network sequence-to-function models (three networks); consensus predictor MADRIGAL
organization: University of California, Berkeley; University of California, San Francisco; Chan Zuckerberg Biohub San Francisco

evidence.tested: 18,750 selected sequences were tested experimentally in yeast; over 90% of 16,770 well-measured sequences functioned as activation domains, and some retained function in fungi, plants and human cells.
evidence.unknown: Not stated in the reviewed material beyond the abstract; functional retention across species is reported for only some designs.
evidence.ai_role: Neural networks scored sequences generated from known activation-domain-like sequences; high-scoring sequences were selected for experimental validation and the consensus model MADRIGAL was developed.
